decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) early window (365–544) with multi-sample drops and partial recoveries in all axes, possibly indicating superposed temporary offsets or jumps; (2) mid-to-late window (485–664) where a sustained trend emerges in N upward and E/U downward, but with a distinct sharp U-dip (~590–610) lacking clear counterparts, warranting closer inspection of cross-axis consistency.

regions.observation: N-component shows a multi-sample drop (~365–375) followed by a slow rebound and plateau until ~410, then a second abrupt drop (~410–415) with partial recovery; E and U show correlated transient offsets around the same intervals, suggesting possible superposed temporary motion or jump with ambiguous return.

From ~560 onward, N exhibits a sustained monotonic rise (steepening after ~600), while E and U show concurrent gradual declines—cross-axis shape suggests coherent long-term trend onset; however, between ~590–610, U shows a sharp multi-sample dip not mirrored in N/E, hinting at a possible localized offset or opposing transient superposed on the trend.
